en.title: Final Data Positions After Sequential Migrations
en.description:
Initially there are n distinct data positions. In input order, move the data at position from to position to; it is guaranteed that from currently holds data and to currently does not. Output all final positions in ascending order.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m, the second line the initial positions, followed by m lines from to. The original text gave no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤100000, 0≤m≤100000, positions 0..10^9.
en.output: Output the n final positions in strictly ascending order, separated by spaces.
en.explanation: The answers are 3 4, 2 5 and 0; the third example shows that data may move back to a position that was vacated.
hints: Keep the current positions in a set; for each move remove from and add to, then sort at the end.
